open_points.subject: issue_contract_version
open_points.text: - issue_contract_version: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise RefusedError naming the first failing check, in this order: a new slot_id with purpose None, or an existing slot whose purpose differs from a given purpose; port names repeat within a direction; an input port without a disclosure class or an output port with one; a file port without exactly one media type or a value port with one; a value_schema outside the supported subset; no output port; a resource bound that is None, not a positive integer, or above its release ceiling, the refusal naming the field and the ceiling; ports are taken inputs first then outputs, each by name.
open_points.other_text: - issue_contract_version: [VALIDATION_ERROR] The release ceilings are the imported RELEASE_CEILING_WALL_TIME_MS, RELEASE_CEILING_MEMORY_BYTES, RELEASE_CEILING_OUTPUT_BYTES and RELEASE_CEILING_PROCESS_COUNT constants for the fields of the same name; a bound above its ceiling or omitted is refused, never clamped or defaulted; every check after the purpose rule binds only a new version: contract_version_id is computed right after the purpose rule when every bound is given, the ResourceBoundsRequest then read as the ResourceBounds of the ContractVersionContent — a request that omits a bound equals no stored version, whose bounds are all given, so it computes no identity and goes on to the checks, which refuse the omission —, and an existing equal contract version is returned unchanged even when a later release lowered a ceiling below its bounds (A01 rule 4, A20 rule 4).
open_points.question: Must an existing equal contract version whose bound now exceeds a lowered release ceiling be refused as the first passage requires, or returned unchanged as the second passage requires?

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case
open_points.text: - execute_trial_case: [BEHAVIOR] The outcome is the sandbox outcome of the same name; a succeeded execution is passed when the case has no expected outputs or every output's digest equals the expected one, a many file output equal only with the same length and equal digests position by position, and output_mismatch otherwise; a succeeded value output whose canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant makes the outcome contract_violation.
open_points.other_text: - execute_trial_case: [VALIDATION_ERROR] When the sandbox reports detail cleanup_failed the execution is recorded crashed with detail_code cleanup_failed first, and then StopRequiredError is raised so that nothing further runs in the request.
open_points.question: If cleanup_failed accompanies a sandbox outcome other than crashed, must the recorded outcome retain the sandbox outcome of the same name or be changed to crashed?
